lines.japanese: １１月２３日、木曜日。ヤナポリ広場１８時。
lines.english: Thursday, November twenty-third. Six p.m. in Yanapoli Plaza.

lines.japanese: 今日はアレだ、国民の祝日。勤労感謝の日。
lines.english: Today was, what do you call it, a national holiday: Labor Thanksgiving Day.

lines.japanese: 俺もおまえもそこの誰かも、お互いにこう、あなたはとてもよく頑張っているイエイエあなたこそと肩を叩きあう日。
lines.english: A day for me, you, and whoever that was over there to clap one another on the shoulder and go, “You’ve worked so hard.” “No, no, you have.”

lines.japanese: ──ま、だから何だって話。ふぁ～あ。
lines.english: —Not that it meant a damn thing. Yaaawn.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ」
lines.english: “Dora.”

lines.japanese: 腕組みしていつものパイプベンチでうとうと舟を漕いでいたら、澄ました子供の声が短く俺を呼んだ。
lines.english: I had my arms folded and was nodding off on my usual pipe bench when a prim child's voice called my name, crisp and short.

lines.japanese: 「あん？」
lines.english: “Hnh?”

lines.japanese: 夢うつつから顔を上げると、黒ずくめのお人形さんみたいなガキんちょが俺の前に立っていた。金髪、碧眼、頭に花とうさぎさん。
lines.english: I surfaced from my doze. A little kid like a doll dressed all in black stood before me: blond hair, blue eyes, flowers and a bunny on her head.

lines.japanese: 「あー、アリスか。なに。どうしたの」
lines.english: “Oh. Alice. What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「おはよございマス」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 金髪のガキは頭を下げずに、欧米風ハロー感覚で片手を上げた。
lines.english: The blond kid didn't bow. She simply raised one hand in a Western-style hello.

lines.japanese: 「……あ？　ああ、おは……あいや、『こんばんは』」
lines.english: “...Huh? Oh, morn—no. It's ‘good evening.’”

lines.japanese: 休日の柳木原は、近くや遠くの県からも暇人が集まって、いつもよりさらに障害物の多い街になっていた。
lines.english: On holidays, Yanagihara drew idle people from prefectures near and far, turning the city into an even denser obstacle course than usual.

lines.japanese: ごってりしたロリータファッションがハマってる外人のお子様と、兄貴にしては歳も目の色も違いすぎる男。不思議な組み合わせに通行人の視線がちらりちらり。
lines.english: An elaborately dressed foreign child who looked born for the frills, and beside her a man far too old and with the wrong color eyes to pass for her brother. Passersby stole glance after glance at the strange pair.

lines.japanese: あーもー、いちいち見んなよくそ、ウゼぇなあー……ぁふ。
lines.english: Oh, come on. Quit staring every goddamn time. So annoying... yaaawn.

lines.japanese: 俺はでっかいあくびをしながら、腰掛けたまま四肢を伸ばした。俺様の超長い脚をよけて、アリスがぴょっと横に跳んだ。
lines.english: Still seated, I stretched all four limbs through a tremendous yawn. Alice hopped neatly aside to avoid my magnificently long legs.

lines.japanese: 「あー、あのアリスさあ、日本じゃ夜は『こんばんは』っつーの。な。『おはよう』は朝の挨拶なんだよ」
lines.english: “Look, Alice. At night in Japan, you say ‘good evening.’ Got it? ‘Good morning’ is for the morning.”

lines.japanese: 日本語ユーザーの先輩として優しくミステイクを指摘してやると、やつは無愛想な白い顔をぷるぷる左右に振った。
lines.english: As the senior Japanese speaker between us, I gently corrected her mistake. She shook her unsmiling white face from side to side.

lines.japanese: 「ちがう、これぎょーかい用語」
lines.english: “Wrong. This is show-business talk.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　うるせえよ。いいんだよ、そういう局地的なのは覚えなくて」
lines.english: “Huh? Shut up. You don't need to learn weird little industry exceptions like that.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、私は思う遊ぶしたい」
lines.english: “Dora, I think I want do playing.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なに」
lines.english: “Huh? What?”

lines.japanese: 「私は遊ぶしたい、ともに」
lines.english: “I want do playing, together.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ……あー、俺と遊びたいの」
lines.english: “Oh... You want to play with me?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、私はとても好きです、日本的伝統遊戯。たとえばそれは、シリトリィ、アヤトリィ、そしてダルマサンガー・コロンブスなどだ」
lines.english: “Yes. I like very much traditional Japanese games. For example: word chain, cat's cradle, and Daruma Columbus.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ダルマサンガー・コロンブスかあ。あれはちょっとここじゃ出来ねえなあ。ふぁ～あ、んじゃよー、野球拳とか王様ゲームでもやるかァー」
lines.english: “Ah, Daruma Columbus. Can't really play that here. Yaaawn. How about strip rock-paper-scissors or the King Game?”

lines.japanese: 「やきゅ……けん……」
lines.english: “Strip… rock-paper-scissors…”

lines.japanese: アリスはビー玉みたいな青い目をぱちくりさせた。すかさずポケットサイズの英語版日本語辞典を取りだしてめくりだす。いやー、載ってねえだろそれはー。
lines.english: Alice blinked her marble-blue eyes. In an instant, she pulled out a pocket-sized English-Japanese dictionary and started flipping through it. Yeah, that wasn't going to be in there.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、私は理解しないそれを。しかし感じる、大きな興味深さを」
lines.english: “Dora, I do not understand this. But I feel great interest.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あそー。じゃー、あと十年ぐらい経ったらやろうなー」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah? Then we'll play it in about ten years.”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ、私はしたい野球拳を、ただちに」
lines.english: “No. I desire strip rock-paper-scissors immediately.”

lines.japanese: 「いやー、いまやっちゃうとオジサンお巡りさんに怒られちゃうんだわー」
lines.english: “Yeah, if we played it now, the nice policeman would get mad at your old uncle here.”

lines.japanese: ふぅ～あ。こんな無愛想な男と遊びたがるなんて、このプライドの高いお嬢さんは、相変わらず同じ年頃のガキんちょと仲良くできねーのかー。
lines.english: Hwaaaah. If she wanted to play with a surly bastard like me, this proud young lady still couldn't get along with kids her own age.

lines.japanese: 「しょーがねえなァ～あ～っふ」
lines.english: “Guess I got no choooice... Yaaawn.”

lines.japanese: 嫌な共感を覚えた俺は、伸びをしながら立ちあがった。そして首関節をほぐすため、頭を大きく左右へ──
lines.english: Feeling an unpleasant kinship, I stretched as I stood. Then, to loosen the joints in my neck, I rolled my head in a wide arc from side to—

lines.japanese: ──ぎょっとした。アリスに負けないぐらいゴテゴテした黒いワンピースの巨体が、雑踏のなか頭ひとつ抜きでてそびえ立っていた。
lines.english: —I froze. A huge body in a black dress every bit as ornate as Alice's towered a full head above the crowd.

lines.japanese: もちろん目を奪われたのは俺だけじゃないようで、その男は（愛らしい異国の少女とは正反対の意味で）衆人の視線を集めている。
lines.english: I clearly wasn't the only one staring. The man drew every eye around him—for precisely the opposite reason from the adorable foreign girl.

lines.japanese: オウムのようなカラフル頭、白く塗りたくった道化の化粧、そして引きずるほどに長いドレススカート。気にしたくもないけど、ここまでイッちゃってるファッションを見せられて気にするなって方が無理だ。
lines.english: Parrot-bright hair. A clown's face slathered white. A dress skirt long enough to drag on the ground. I desperately wanted not to care, but once fashion went this far off the deep end, not caring was impossible.

lines.japanese: ──あ、やっべ、ツレの女と目が合っちゃった。
lines.english: —Oh, shit. I'd made eye contact with the woman he was with.

lines.japanese: オウム男に連れそっていたのは、バレーボール選手みたいにタッパのある大女。頭の位置は俺よりも高そうだ。手入れの行きとどいた艶めく黒髪が、右目を覆いつつまっすぐケツあたりまで流れおちている。
lines.english: The woman with Parrot Man was built like a volleyball player, tall enough that her head seemed to rise above mine. Meticulously tended black hair gleamed as it covered her right eye and fell straight to her ass.

lines.japanese: たっぷり全身を包む真っ黒いコートとの組み合わせは、巨漢の女装男ほどでないにせよ、それでも十二分に奇抜なファッション（つーか、なんかのコスプレなのかも）だ。
lines.english: Combined with the voluminous black coat swallowing her from head to toe, it wasn't quite as extreme as the giant man in drag, but it was still spectacularly eccentric. Maybe it was some kind of costume.
“What is it...?”

lines.japanese: そいつは伸びすぎた長い髪をばっさり割って、お化け屋敷のお岩さんみたいに肩をすぼめて近付いてきた。いや、来んなよ。こえーよ。
lines.english: She parted the overgrown curtain of hair and approached with her shoulders hunched like the ghost Oiwa in a haunted house. No. Don't come over. You're terrifying.

lines.japanese: 「なに見てんの」
lines.english: “What're you looking at?”

lines.japanese: 「いえいえ。見てない見てない」
lines.english: “Nothing, nothing. Wasn't looking.”

lines.japanese: 俺は首を直角に曲げてそっぽ向き、右手だけを正面でぱたぱた振った。
lines.english: I snapped my head ninety degrees to the side and flapped my right hand in denial.

lines.japanese: 関わりたくない。こんな怪しげな連中には関わりたくない。いや、そりゃあ、ひとを外見で判断するのは良くないけどさ、にしたってコレは……なあ？
lines.english: I wanted no involvement. None whatsoever with people this suspicious. Sure, judging people by appearances was wrong, but this was... I mean, come on.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、いま僕らのこと見てたよね」
lines.english: “Hey. You were looking at us just now, weren't you?”

lines.japanese: 掠れた笛を吹くような、細い声音が降ってきた。俺は顎が鎖骨に付きそうなぐらい深く俯いた。
lines.english: A thin voice like a hoarse flute drifted down. I bowed my head so deeply my chin nearly touched my collarbone.

lines.japanese: 「誤解誤解。全然全然」
lines.english: “You've got it wrong. Totally. Completely.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、見てたよ。世俗の価値観で濁ったレンズに僕らの声なき愁訴を映していたよ」
lines.english: “No. You looked. Through a lens clouded by the values of the vulgar world, you reflected our voiceless lament.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 耳慣れない日本語に、うっかり顔を上げてしまった。自分を僕と呼ぶ女は、号泣一歩手前の形相で俺を見下ろしていた。
lines.english: The unfamiliar Japanese made me look up despite myself. The woman, who referred to herself like a boy, looked down at me with a face one step short of sobbing.

lines.japanese: 容貌は美人なのかどうなのか微妙な、国内より海外で評価される個性派女優みたいだった。そんな女に涙目で絡まれるんだ、これはもう、ある意味ヤクザのいちゃもんより恐い。
lines.english: I couldn't quite tell whether she was beautiful—she had the face of one of those distinctive actresses appreciated more overseas than at home. Being confronted through tears by a woman like that was, in a way, scarier than a gangster picking a fight.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、なんで見てたの？」
lines.english: “Why were you looking?”

lines.japanese: 「いや見てないって」
lines.english: “I said I wasn't.”

lines.japanese: 「なんでそんなに凍える息吹を吹きかけるの？」
lines.english: “Why do you breathe such a freezing breath upon us?”

lines.japanese: 「だから見てな……え、なに？」
lines.english: “I wasn't look—wait, what?”

lines.japanese: 「シロツメクサの草原に咲いてしまったパンジーはどれほどの白眼視を浴びれば染まれるというの？」
lines.english: “How many cold stares must the pansy that bloomed in a field of white clover endure before it can take on their color?”

lines.japanese: 「あイヤ、どーっすかねえ……あー、それはちょっと……自分わかんないっすねえ……」
lines.english: “Uh, yeah, I dunno... That's, uh... I'm really not sure about that one...”

lines.japanese: なんだよ勘弁しろよ、やべえよこいつ、キモチ悪りいよ。アレか、電波っつーか、いわゆるキ印さんか。
lines.english: Oh, come on, spare me. This one was bad. Creepy as hell. Was she one of those people tuned to a private frequency? A certified nutcase?

lines.japanese: 参った。さすがに張っ倒すワケいかねーし（つうか、ちょと押した程度じゃ倒れなさそうだこの壁女）、だからってこんなん相手してたって時間の無駄だ。
lines.english: Great. I couldn't exactly knock her flat—and this wall of a woman didn't look like she'd fall over from a little shove anyway—but dealing with her was a waste of time.

lines.japanese: しゃーない、とりあえずアリスを連れて、さっさとどっかへ──
lines.english: Fine. I'd take Alice and get the hell somewhere—
“—what the?!”

lines.japanese: とつぜん女に両肩を掴まれた。身長を活かしてハンドボールでもやってるのか、およそ女とは思えない握力だった。こえええ。俺がいまひとりだったら確実に逃げてる。
lines.english: The woman suddenly seized both my shoulders. Maybe she put that height to use playing handball; her grip was nothing you'd expect from a woman. Terrifying. If I'd been alone, I would already have run.

lines.japanese: 「どうなの！　ねえ、君が嘲笑っているのは埋もれざる個性？　それとも浮き足立つ群像？　ひどいよ、ねえＲ－ウィングの何を嘲笑っていたの！」
lines.english: “Which is it? Tell me! Are you mocking the individuality that refuses to be buried, or the masses who have lost their footing? It’s cruel! What part of R-Wing were you laughing at?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょちょちょ、痛い痛い、放せって。なんだよ、なにＲなんたらって。知らねえよ、なんだこれ、ギャグか。あ、ドッキリか。おー、カメラどこだカメラ」
lines.english: “Whoa, whoa, that hurts. Let go. What the hell is R-whatever? Never heard of it. What is this, a joke? Oh, a hidden-camera prank? All right, where's the camera?”

lines.japanese: そして俺は、デカい女に見下ろされながら揺すぶられる一方で──
lines.english: And while the enormous woman looked down and shook me—

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、遊ぶー」
lines.english: “Dora, play.”

lines.japanese: ──小さい女に見上げられながら抱きつかれていた。
lines.english: —the little one looked up and clung to me.

lines.japanese: アリスは込みいった日本語が理解できないせいか、黒ずくめの幽霊女など気にも留めていなかった。むしろ取られたおもちゃを奪いかえさんとする勢いで、俺の体に固くしがみついている。
lines.english: Maybe because she couldn't follow the complicated Japanese, Alice paid no attention to the ghost woman in black. If anything, she clutched me with the determination of a child reclaiming a stolen toy.

lines.japanese: 「遊ぶ遊ぶー、遊ぶしてください、ともにー」
lines.english: “Play, play. Please do playing, together.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえ答えて！　なんで見たの、放火魔の悦楽が君の外眼筋を衝きうごかしているの！」
lines.english: “Answer me! Why did you look? Does an arsonist's ecstasy drive your extraocular muscles?”

lines.japanese: 女ふたり同時にベタつかれるという状況で、こんなにも嬉しくないと思ったのは初めてだった。
lines.english: Never before had being pawed by two women at once brought me so little joy.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、あなたは生まれた、遊ぶために私で。だから、あなたは生きてない、遊ばないとき私で」
lines.english: “Dora, you were born for playing by me. Therefore, you do not live when you do not play by me.”

lines.japanese: 「いやちょっと待てってアリス、な、いまオッチャン、恐いひとに絡まれてる最中だから。な、ほら、あっちでマルチネスと遊んでなさい」
lines.english: “Hold on, Alice. I'm in the middle of getting harassed by a scary person. Go play with Martinez over there, okay?”

lines.japanese: 俺はまず与しやすい方の女から説得を始めた。しかし──
lines.english: I started by negotiating with the more manageable woman. But—

lines.japanese: 「キョーヤ、何してんの」
lines.english: “Kyoya, what are you doing?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ミチヤ」
lines.english: “Oh, Michiya.”

lines.japanese: ──先に離れてくれたのは電波な方の女だった。
lines.english: —the woman on the alien frequency was the first to let go.

lines.japanese: 「あのね、この子が僕らを蔑んでた」
lines.english: “Listen. This boy was looking down on us.”

lines.japanese: やつは父親に告げ口する子供みたいに、俺を指差しながら後ろを向いた。
lines.english: Like a child tattling to her father, she turned around and pointed at me.

lines.japanese: 「うん？　それはよくないね」
lines.english: “Hmm? That isn't very nice.”

lines.japanese: 女の後ろに、またひとつ長身がそびえていた。背は高いけど、顔はひどく不健康そうな男。たっぷりした軍用コートの下には、ぴっちりしたモッズスーツが見えた。
lines.english: Another figure loomed behind her, tall and sickly-looking. Beneath a voluminous military coat, I glimpsed a skin-tight mod suit.

lines.japanese: なんとなく、ビートルズ世代のとっぽい兄ちゃんみたいだ。何十年だか前のイギリスには、こんな格好で夜な夜なモノコックボディのスクーターを乗りまわす反社会的なモダンボーイズがたくさんいたらしい。
lines.english: He looked like a Mod straight out of the Beatles era. Britain decades ago was apparently full of antisocial young men dressed like that, roaring around at night on pressed-steel scooters.

lines.japanese: やつは神経質にネクタイの結び目を調整しながら、俺を見下ろして陰気な声で告げる。
lines.english: He nervously adjusted the knot of his tie, looked down at me, and spoke in a gloomy voice.

lines.japanese: 「謝った？　早く謝った方がいいよ、こう見えて彼女は怒ると恐いんだ」
lines.english: “Did you apologize? You should hurry. She may not look it, but she's frightening when she's angry.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なに、聞こえねえよ。ごにょごにょ言ってねえで腹から声出せ」
lines.english: “Huh? What? Can't hear you. Quit mumbling and speak from the gut.”

lines.japanese: 相手の一方的で恐喝じみた言い草を、俺は真っ向から打ちかえした。
lines.english: I met his one-sided, vaguely extortionate demand head-on.

lines.japanese: 「へえ……随分と生意気な口を利く……」
lines.english: “My... what an impertinent way of speaking...”

lines.japanese: モッズ野郎はカラーコンタクトに覆われた青い瞳で、ねちっこく俺を眺めまわす。眼球の周りが落ちくぼんだ、睡眠障害の病人みたいな目。睫毛の下には色の濃いくまが浮いていた。
lines.english: The mod bastard inspected me at length through blue contact lenses. His eyes were sunken like those of a sick man starved of sleep, with dark shadows beneath the lashes.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、いいや……かわいい妹さんに免じて赦してあげるよ……」
lines.english: “Well, never mind... I'll forgive you for the sake of your adorable little sister...”

lines.japanese: 俺がシカトして宙を睨んでいると、やつはアリスのはちみつ色をした頭に手をかざした。直に触れようものならソッコー払いのけてやろうと身構えたが、モッズ野郎はそうせず、手を下ろして仲間の女へ向きなおった。
lines.english: I ignored him and glared into empty space. He held a hand over Alice's honey-colored head. I braced myself to knock it away the instant he touched her, but the mod bastard lowered it without doing so and turned back to the woman.

lines.japanese: 「キョーヤ、猊下が呼んでる。はやく来て」
lines.english: “Kyoya, His Eminence is calling. Hurry.”

lines.japanese: 「猊下が？　うん、分かった」
lines.english: “His Eminence? All right.”

lines.japanese: そのたった一言で、イカれた幽霊女は何事もなかったかのように、はたはたとオウム頭のもとへ駆けもどっていった。
lines.english: At those few words, the lunatic ghost woman pattered back to Parrot Head as though nothing had happened.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあね、お嬢ちゃん」
lines.english: “Goodbye, young lady.”

lines.japanese: 男もあとに続く。
lines.english: The man followed.

lines.japanese: 黒い背中がふたつオウム男のもとへ戻ると、やつらは三人連れだってしずしずと駅ビル方面へ歩きだした。祝日の夜を不気味にそぞろ歩く、背高ノッポの仮装行列。俺は鼻息を吹いた。
lines.english: Once the two black-clad figures rejoined Parrot Man, the three began a stately walk toward the station building: a towering costume parade taking an eerie holiday-evening stroll. I snorted.

lines.japanese: 「なんだありゃ」
lines.english: “What the hell was that?”

lines.japanese: 柳木原は広い。一部じゃああいう格好が流行ってるんだろうか。俺は前にああいう集団を見たときのことを思いかえした。
lines.english: Yanagihara was a big place. Maybe that look was fashionable in one corner of it. I thought back to the last time I'd seen a group like that.

lines.japanese: ハリュー・クロードの華麗なる太鼓ショウ。実はいまの三人も、あのときあの場に居合わせていたかもしれない。
lines.english: Haryu Claude's magnificent drum show. Come to think of it, those three might have been there that day, too.

lines.japanese: ん……そういえばあのジェンベ、今日も聞こえてこないな……。
lines.english: Hmm... and now that I thought about it, the djembe wasn't sounding tonight either...

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、あそぶ私と」
lines.english: “Dora, play by me.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、おう」
lines.english: “Oh. Right.”

lines.japanese: 強く揺さぶられて我に返った。濁っていない蒼目がじっと俺を見上げている。さすが大陸産、天然ものは輝きが違う。
lines.english: She shook me hard, bringing me back to myself. Unclouded blue eyes gazed steadily up at me. Straight from the Continent; natural specimens really did shine differently.

lines.japanese: 俺は子供の我侭さに呆れるやら感心するやらで、仕方ない相手してやるかという気になった。
lines.english: I was torn between exasperation and admiration at the child's selfishness, and finally decided I might as well humor her.

lines.japanese: 「いいけどおまえ、マルチネスの手伝いは──」
lines.english: “Fine, but aren't you supposed to be helping Martinez—”

lines.japanese: アリスの保護者に一声かけるべく、アクセサリー商の姿を探した。
lines.english: I searched for the accessory seller, meaning to have a word with Alice's guardian.

lines.japanese: 「──あれ。なに、今日マルチネスいねーの。あいつ、どしたん」
lines.english: “—wait. Martinez isn't here today? What happened to him?”

lines.japanese: いつも露店があるあたりを見渡しながら尋ねた。するとアリスは俺の体からパッと離れて背中を向けた。
lines.english: I looked around the spot where his stall usually stood as I asked. Alice abruptly released me and turned her back.

lines.japanese: 「キンロカンシャ、キンロカンシャ……キンロカンシャ……」
lines.english: “Labor Thanks... Labor Thanksgiving... Labor Thanksgiving...”

lines.japanese: ポケット辞典を小さく開いてこっそり発声練習。向きなおるや髪を掻きあげ得意げに披露。
lines.english: She opened her pocket dictionary just a crack and quietly practiced the pronunciation. Then she turned back, swept back her hair, and presented it proudly.

lines.japanese: 「キンロカンシャの日」
lines.english: “Labor Thanksgiving Day.”

lines.japanese: 「発音うまいな」
lines.english: “Great pronunciation.”

lines.japanese: 「どういたします」
lines.english: “You welcome.”

lines.japanese: 誉めてやるとアリスは片手を上げ、嬉しそうに小鼻を膨らませた。
lines.english: At the compliment, Alice raised one hand and flared her nostrils happily.

lines.japanese: 「はあ。つまりマルチネスの休業してる理由が勤労感謝の日だと」
lines.english: “Right. So Martinez is closed because it's Labor Thanksgiving Day.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、そうだ」
lines.english: “Yes. That is so.”

lines.japanese: 「何あいつ。え、ああいう商売って休日こそ稼ぎどきだろ。勤労してねーじゃん、全然してねーじゃん」
lines.english: “What’s with that guy? Isn’t a holiday exactly when a business like his should make the most money? He’s not laboring at all. Not even a little.”

lines.japanese: 「いいえ。あなたは言えない、ヒトノコト」
lines.english: “No. You cannot say this of other people.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「なぜなら、あなたはむしょく」
lines.english: “Because you are unemployed.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　んだてめ、ろくでもねー単語ばっか覚えやがって……無職なめんな、ファックすんぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Huh? The hell? You keep learning all the worst goddamn words… Don't underestimate the unemployed. I'll fuck you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「やれるものならやってみなさい、この無職童貞カスだらけの短小包茎×んこ」
lines.english: “Try it if you can, you jobless virgin with a tiny, smegma-caked, foreskin-choked dick.”

lines.japanese: 「え、えええっ！？」
lines.english: “W-what?!”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょ待っ……お、おま、おまえ、そんな、そんなこと言って恥ずかしくねーのかよ……」
lines.english: “W-wait… Y-you… Aren't you embarrassed saying shit like that?”

lines.japanese: 「おびただしく平気。なぜなら、私は把握しない、その言葉が持つところの微妙なニュアンス」
lines.english: “I am profusely fine. Because I do not grasp delicate nuances which those words possess.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、どんなスラング辞典見たのか知んねーけど、ぜんぜん微妙じゃねえからソレ。バリ直球だから」
lines.english: “I don't know what kind of slang dictionary you found, but there ain't anything delicate about that. It's a fastball straight down the middle.”

lines.japanese: あと、おびただしいの使い方間違ってる。
lines.english: And she'd used *profusely* wrong.

lines.japanese: 「いいえ、私はとても恥ずかしくない。×んこ×んこ極太×んこ。黒くてぶっとい絶倫×んこ」
lines.english: “No. I am very not embarrassed. D*ck, d*ck, extra-thick d*ck. Big black tireless d*ck.”

lines.japanese: 「うお、すげえ。外人すげえ。無敵じゃんおまえ、倫理協会ドンと来いじゃん」
lines.english: “Whoa. Foreigners are incredible. You're invincible. Bring on the ethics board.”

lines.japanese: 「え、なに、そんじゃ『私の奥までじゅぷじゅぷ熱いの注ぎこんでください』とかも言えちゃうわけ」
lines.english: “So you could even say, ‘Please squirt the hot stuff into me, all the way deep inside’?”

lines.japanese: 「もちろんだ、私は言えるに違いない」
lines.english: “Of course. I must certainly be able.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。じゃ言ってみ」
lines.english: “Seriously? Go on, then.”

lines.japanese: 「わた、わたたのっ」
lines.english: “I-into… into me…”

lines.japanese: 「えー、駄目じゃん。やっぱ恥ずかしいんじゃん」
lines.english: “Nope, no good. You *are* embarrassed.”

lines.japanese: 「お、おくおく、おく、おくまでっ……」
lines.english: “D-deep, deep… all the way inside…”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いいって。いいっておまえ、そんな無理すんなって」
lines.english: “Forget it. Seriously, don't force yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「も、問題ない。それはとてもたやすいことだ」
lines.english: “N-no problem. It is a very easy thing.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。すげえ、おまえガキのくせにハンパねー度胸だな。そういうの日本語で大和魂っつんだよ。よし分かった、応援してやる。がんばれアリス」
lines.english: “Seriously? Damn, you've got incredible nerve for a kid. In Japanese, we call that the Japanese spirit. All right, I get it. I'll cheer you on. You can do it, Alice.”

lines.japanese: 「じゅじゅっ、じゅぷ、じゅぷ……」
lines.english: “S-squ… squirt, squirt…”

lines.japanese: 「おーし、がんばれ。もう一息。ほら、もう一声」
lines.english: “That's it. Keep going. Almost there. One more push.”

lines.japanese: 「あつっ、あつあつ、熱いのっ……」
lines.english: “The h-hot… the hot stuff…”

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん……？」
lines.english: “Dora...?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なんだよ、っせえな。ちょっと待ってろ、いま大事なとこだから──」
lines.english: “Huh? What? Shut up and wait, we're at the important part—”

lines.japanese: 「──って、なんだプラチナかよ。なに、どうしたの」
lines.english: “—oh, it's you, Platinum. What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「あの、あなた……いたいけな子供に何を言わせようと……」
lines.english: “Um… What exactly are you trying to make this innocent child say?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「熱いのじゅぶじゅぶ注ぎこんでくださいっ！」
lines.english: “Please squirt the hot stuff deep inside me!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、ちげって。ちょちょちょ、誤解すんなよ？　だってコレ、こいつが勝手に自分から──」
lines.english: “No, wait, it ain't like that. Don't get the wrong idea, okay? She started all this herself—”

lines.japanese: 「男はみんなそう言うわ」
lines.english: “That is what all men say.”

lines.japanese: 「──おまえ、日本語覚える順番ぜってー間違ってるって」
lines.english: “—you are definitely learning Japanese in the wrong order.”
